propositions: Whole-tree fixture helpers exported 3,019 checkout files instead of the minimal three files (hatch_build.py, pyproject.toml, src/rebar/__init__.py) required by production hook, causing redundant package builds on all three xdist workers and consuming 56+ seconds per run.

Artifact-probe workflow used trusted-main GITHUB_SHA instead of git rev-parse --short HEAD after final checkout and asserted truthiness rather than exact SHA equality, allowing patchset 9aecb53e to build with wrong commit 7d908fb and violating exact-source identity contract.

Per-worker fixture setup initialization fell from 6.60-6.74s to 2.20-2.88s (56-67% improvement) and focused serial build time fell from 18.23s to 9.11s (50% improvement) by eliminating whole-tree materialization and using a minimal real-hook Hatch package with isolated PEP 517 boundary.

Production hatch_build.py on the minimal committed package fixture preserved env override, Git fallback, blank-env failure, sdist preservation, and shallow-source behaviors while eliminating three redundant full builds across matrix cells.

Both artifact workflow lanes (_artifact-probe.yml for branch-head and Gerrit patchset checkouts) must derive REBAR_EXPECTED_COMMIT from git rev-parse --short HEAD after final checkout and require exact wheel and sdist equality instead of truthiness probes.
